evidence: createApp registers Express routes and only calls OrderService methods (addProduct, placeOrder, transitionOrder, cancelOrder, etc.), with no business logic inline.
The error-handling middleware maps NotFoundError to 404, InsufficientStockError/DomainError to 409 and SyntaxError to 400. This is transport-level error translation.
objectBody, stringField, numberField and parseItems check the type and shape of the request body. This is HTTP input parsing.
parseState only checks membership in orderStates. Transition rules are not in this file.
The default parameter `new OrderService(new InMemoryFulfilmentStore())` is composition/wiring, which fits the infrastructure layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts is an Express transport adapter, and everything in it is infrastructure work. It sets up routes and JSON body parsing. It checks that request bodies have the right shape (objectBody, stringField, numberField, parseItems, parseState), passes each call on to OrderService, and turns errors into HTTP status codes. It also sets up a default composition with InMemoryFulfilmentStore. None of the route handlers holds business rules. Stock checks, order state transitions and cancellation logic all stay in OrderService or the domain. parseState only checks that the input is one of the known orderStates values. It does not decide which transitions are allowed. One small point: the request-shape checks throw DomainError, so transport validation errors share a type with domain errors. This muddies the error types but does not move a business responsibility into this file, so it is not a violation.
